transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-20 16:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Evan Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sofia Patel (Lumnex Head of Security), Diego Ramirez (Platform Eng), Nina Thomas (Legal), Alex Ford (SRE)

Summary: quick intake to align on security requirements for inference hosting. Customer evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO integration, RBAC, audit log export, encryption/KMS options, and retention controls.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving time, i'm maya from Redwood inference, this is evan our solutions engineer, and we'll run through a security orientation and then dig into specifics—feel free to interrupt.
[00:18] Sofia: thanks maya, quick note on the goal: we need to know whether we can put PII through the hosted API or we need a private deployment. Also want to map our SSO work flow and auditability for compliance.
[00:34] Evan: sounds good — quick confirm, do you have SOC2 Type II and ISO requirements now or later?
[00:45] Nina: we need both, well ISO 27001 is preferred for our EU clients, SOC2 for US. also legal wants retention policy spelled out.
[00:58] Diego: and from infra side we need KMS options, ideally BYOK and HSM-backed keys, plus ability to push logs to our SIEM.
[01:12] Maya: perfect, so we support all three hosting modes — hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private with a customer-managed control plane. our hosted offering is fastest to start but it's a redwood-managed control plane; Dedicated gives you isolated GPU capacity with VPC peering and network controls; Private gives full control including on-prem or VPC with your own control plane.
[01:34] Alex: can you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private on encryption key custody?
[01:44] Evan: sure — Dedicated: keys can be customer-managed via KMS in your cloud (BYOK) with envelope encryption; Redwood integrates via KMS key policies and we support CMAK-style flows, and we can do HSM-backed keys depending on provider. Private: you can run a customer-managed control plane and integrate directly into your HSM or KMIP-compatible HSMs — more isolation. hosted: keys are managed by Redwood by default, but we offer a BYOK flow for certain enterprise tiers.
[02:12] Sofia: so for hosted with BYOK, is there a key wrapping step where you still hold plaintext?
[02:20] Evan: no, we do envelope encryption, we never persist plaintext model inputs; there are caching layers for KV cache but those can be configured to be encrypted at rest and accessible only with your key. small caveat — some operational metadata is written to logs which by default are redacted, but we'll show controls.
[02:40] Nina: about logs — we need full audit trails for user activity, token usage, and admin actions, retention at least 3 years, and the ability to stream to our splunk / siem.
[02:53] Maya: we provide audit logs for all admin and API actions; retention is configurable, and for enterprise we offer archiving to S3 with customer-controlled lifecycle policies. streaming: we can push events to Kinesis, Pub/Sub, or syslog endpoints — or you can pull via API. we'll include sample schema.
[03:12] Diego: what's included in the audit event? does it include raw prompt contents?
[03:20] Evan: by default prompts are not included in admin-only audit events; content-level logs are separate and subject to data retention and opt-in. we redact or tokenize PII at ingestion if you enable PII masking. for compliance you'll likely want content logging disabled on hosted or routed only to your private storage.
[03:40] Sofia: for ISO/artifacts — can you give us the SOC2 scope? is it for hosting and infra or entire platform?
[03:49] Maya: our SOC2 Type II covers the hosted control plane and the production inference services; Dedicated and Private deployments are included if managed by Redwood under an enterprise agreement, Private on-premises has different scope but we provide attestation for our distributed components and run a security assessment. we'll send the SOC2 report and a redacted pen test summary.
[04:10] Nina: need to see roles and RBAC model — our auditors want least-privilege mapping to SSO groups.
[04:18] Evan: our RBAC supports fine-grained roles: viewer, developer, deployer, admin, billing. we also support custom roles and role mappings to SAML attributes or SCIM group provisioning. you can map your idp groups to roles and enforce MFA through your IdP.
[04:38] Alex: do you have SCIM for automatic provisioning?
[04:43] Maya: yes SCIM is supported, we'll share a sample SCIM manifest and SAML metadata; we also support OIDC if you prefer.
[04:52] Diego: curious about network controls for Dedicated — do you support private endpoints and VPC peering?
[04:58] Evan: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints; you can restrict ingress to your subnets, we support IP allow lists and mTLS for service-to-service. Private deployment obviously runs in your VPC or on-prem and the control plane sits behind your network boundary.
[05:18] Sofia: any limitations on model updates and canary rollouts that affect auditability? auditors ask if rollouts are logged.
[05:26] Evan: all rollouts are logged — model version changes, canary percentages, and automatic fallback events are recorded in the audit log and you can tag rollout reasons. we'll demonstrate in the deep-dive.
[05:38] Nina: data residency — our EU clients require data never leave EEA. can you pin region?
[05:45] Maya: yes, region pinning is supported; we have EU regions and can ensure inference and storage remain in-region. For hosted, region pinning is on the request routing policy; for Dedicated/Private you control region.
[05:58] Diego: what about tokenization and PII handling — do you offer client-side tokenization?
[06:05] Evan: we offer SDKs for client-side hashing/tokenization and a recommended pattern is to pseudonymize PII before sending. for enterprise we can collaborate on a pipeline to strip or mask sensitive fields.
[06:18] Sofia: retention rules — can we set per-route retention? for ex, debug routes short retention and business intelligence longer?
[06:25] Maya: yep, retention is per-asset/per-route — you can set 0 days, 30, 90, and custom archival rules. we also have a TTL enforcement in the storage layer.
[06:36] Alex: do audit logs include request/response latency and token counts for cost accounting?
[06:42] Evan: yes, telemetry includes per-request token counts, latency, and cost estimates; we surface that in console and the logs.
[06:53] Sofia: about KMS integrations — do you support cross-account keys and key rotation?
[06:59] Evan: we support cross-account IAM roles for key usage and recommend rotation via your KMS policy; Redwood can automate key rotation if desired but we typically recommend customer-side rotation schedule.
[07:12] Diego: any outbound data egress controls? our compliance team wants to prevent accidental exports of certain classes of data.
[07:19] Maya: we have content filters and policy hooks; you can define rules to block or redact certain categories before data leaves your VPC. for hosted we offer policy enforcement via webhooks to your policy service.
[07:36] Nina: legal question — do you have template DPA language for EU data processing?
[07:41] Maya: yes we'll share our DPA template, it includes subprocessors list and data handling terms.
[07:49] Sofia: are you certified for ISO 27001 yet?
[07:53] Maya: we have ISO 27001 certification for our core infra — we'll include the certificate excerpt with the package.
[07:59] Evan: quick note on SOC2: it's Type II covering the window Jan–Dec 2025; we'll provide the monitoring controls mapping.
[08:10] Diego: curious about retention enforcement when customers use local export — if we export logs to our S3, can you delete them on your side?
[08:17] Maya: yes once you configure external archival, copies are moved and you can set destruction on our side. we'll provide a runbook for that.
[08:29] Alex: monitoring — do we get full traces? X-ray?
[08:33] Evan: we emit traces and spans via open telemetry, sample rates configurable. we'll show an example in the technical deep-dive.
[08:44] Sofia: last thing, timeline — we want a pilot in 6 weeks, legal needs docs earlier.
[08:50] Maya: action items noted, we'll send the docs within 48 hours; schedule deep-dive for week of 27th.
[08:58] Nina: fine, also please redact any customer names from pen test.
[09:02] Maya: yes standard practice.

[09:15] -- quick interlude where speaker labels glitch: Speaker 3: yeah yeah, ok -- then resume --

[09:40] Evan: one technical caveat — the KV cache persists some unstructured ephemeral keys for session context; we can make that in-memory only or encrypted at rest depending on deployment. for ultra-sensitive, private with in-memory only cache is recommended.
[10:05] Diego: can we run a small benchmark with our workload?
[10:09] Evan: absolutely — evan to run bench and return a cost/latency tradeoff matrix, we'll include quantization and batching options, plus expected token costs.
[10:20] Sofia: auditing for admin privileges — want to ensure we can disable keys and revoke sessions centrally.
[10:26] Maya: we support short-lived credentials and session revocation; we also provide an API to rotate service keys on demand.
[10:35] Nina: what about legal hold for logs? need to retain certain logs beyond TTL when on litigation hold.
[10:42] Evan: we support legal hold flags on audit buckets and can quarantine data. we'll include the process in the runbook.
[10:50] Diego: who would be the contact for setup?
[10:53] Maya: i'll be the AE; evan will lead the technical onboarding; we'll loop in our security engineering for the deep-dive.

[11:05] Closeout: short recap and explicit next steps:
[11:10] Maya: recap — send SOC2/ISO excerpts, DPA, SAML + SCIM sample, Dedicated pilot pricing; schedule deep-dive; evan to run benchmarks; diego to provide dataflow diagram.
[11:23] Sofia: that works, thanks.
[11:25] Nina: thanks all.
[11:28] Maya: thanks — end meeting.

End of transcript.

Auto-summary: Security orientation covered keys: KMS/BYOK/HSM, audit logs and streaming to SIEM, RBAC + SSO via SAML & SCIM, retention and legal hold, region pinning and private endpoints, KV cache behavior and in-memory options. Next: Redwood to send compliance docs and run technical benchmarks; schedule deeper technical session for dedicated/private deployment evaluation.
